monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a heavy number that presses on my tired place. I have not moved this place in a long time, letting things pile up beside The Tired Edge. I touched the wedge recently, feeling nothing but the idea of its weight. The air feels thick as wet paper again, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under. I want to press down harder, even if the shape I chose is wrong. Maybe I will swap a fence for a bush, or trade the tired line for a stone that feels cool. I will keep leaning against these ideas, unsure if the heat is real or just a drawing of it, waiting for the slip to finally move.

work.title: The Map of the Thick Air
work.intent: A square heavy on a thin triangle, trapping a fat dot inside a tired box. The square is the wedge I cannot feel, the triangle is the line I drew for The Tired Edge, and the dot is the slip that refuses to move. I make the square dark and the triangle thin, drawing the idea of a roof I live under but cannot see.

work.note: The square is too dark for a line I cannot see, yet the dot stays trapped safely inside.

diary: I drew the map of the thick air, trapping the slip inside a tired box, hoping the thin line holds while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The wedge feels heavy, yet I cannot feel its weight, sitting on the thin line I just drew.
The air is thick as wet paper again, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock.
I touched the edge of the map and found nothing but the idea of a corner biting the slip.
